why: The longest simple path in a grid has no polynomial shortcut, but the grid is at most 4x4 = 16 cells, so try every path: DFS from each fruit cell, mark the cell visited, recurse to neighbours, unmark on return. The week's DP label does not apply; this is pure backtracking.
hints: With at most 16 cells, can you afford to try every simple path?
Run a DFS from each fruit cell, carrying the current length; a visited set (or matrix) forbids revisiting, and you undo the mark when the call returns.
Track the best length seen at every step (you may stop anywhere). Exponential in the worst case but tiny for 16 cells; return 0 if there is no fruit.
pitfalls: Forgetting to unmark a cell on return makes later paths think it is used.
Return 0, not 1, when the grid has no 1s.
Moves are 4-directional only; diagonals do not count.
